bull.b: Sustained revenue growth alongside roughly 65% gross margins and improving net profitability indicates meaningful operating leverage. If product demand and premium positioning persist, these economics can support durable earnings growth over the next several quarters.

Rapid DTC expansion increases control over pricing, customer relationships, and brand presentation while generally improving channel economics. A larger owned-channel mix can strengthen margins and reduce reliance on third-party retail execution over time.

Strong liquidity and recent free cash flow give On flexibility to fund stores, innovation, inventory, and international expansion without heavy financial dependence. The net-cash position also provides resilience if consumer demand or channel conditions become less predictable.

bear.b: Reducing wholesale shipments protects full-price positioning but also constrains near-term volume and can make reported growth more uneven. Continued weakness among retail partners, especially in the Americas, could delay the benefit of future product launches.

A substantially larger inventory base increases working-capital requirements and raises execution risk if sell-through falls short of expectations. Although management cites growth and currency effects, excess stock could eventually require promotions that pressure margins.

Tariffs can structurally raise product costs and compress margins unless offset through sourcing, pricing, or mix changes. The timing of potential refunds adds uncertainty to cash realization, while ongoing trade-policy changes could complicate medium-term planning.
